prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
adoption/redesign changes are helpful, with 3 winning tests agreeing on positive impact (+7.1% average after noise correction).
sign_in/hint changes are helpful, with 2 winning tests agreeing on positive impact, though 2 later tests showed no clear effect (+2.9% average after noise correction).
choose_path/copy changes showed no clear effect across 2 tests.
home/new_screen changes showed no clear effect across 2 tests.
Evidence is still thin for choose_path/layout, finish/new_flow, finish/new_screen, finish/notification, home/wait_info, and sign_in/reorder as each has only one test.
Predictions were overstated in Round 1 and for weak ideas, but significantly underestimated major winners in adoption/redesign and sign_in/hint.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, redesign: +7.1% after noise correction, 3 test(s)
- choose_path, copy: -2.1% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- choose_path, layout: -3.9% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, new_flow: -6.8% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, new_screen: +1.1% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, notification: +0.3% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- home, new_screen: -0.8% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- home, wait_info: -1.5% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, hint: +2.9% after noise correction, 4 test(s)
- sign_in, reorder: -6.9% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 82.1%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 85.3%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 28.1%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [sign_in, reorder] Delay Sign-In After Adoption Certificate Step: Move the sign-in step to immediately after the adoption certificate screen so users sign in only after completing pet adoption. (why: Signing in early causes dropoff (82.1% conversion); completing adoption first creates strong emotional commitment before account setup.)
1: [sign_in, hint] Cloud Sync and Account Safety Hint: Add explicit hint text on the sign-in screen reassuring users that signing in protects their pet from data loss or reset. (why: Support logged 8 emails about pets missing or reset after signing in, and sign-in hints have historically proven effective (+2.9% average).)
2: [finish, copy] Desktop Companion Activation Headline Copy Update: Update the home intro headline and body text to clearly explain how to reveal the desktop pet and access taskbar controls. (why: Finish step drop-off is 64.8% and support has 3 emails asking how to hide, control, or talk to the pet after onboarding.)
3: [adoption, incentive] Express Hatching Companion Incentive Banner: Add an instant desktop activation badge to the adoption certificate screen encouraging quick completion. (why: Adoption step duration is long (mean 1017s); reinforcing instant availability incentivizes users to complete setup.)
4: [home, notification] Desktop Ready System Tray Sound Notification: Play a subtle chime and send a desktop ready system tray alert when background initialization completes on the waiting screen. (why: The waiting screen has a very high mean duration (2336s) suggesting users tab away while waiting for pet rendering.)

scores.note: Reordering sign-in previously showed negative lift (-6.9%) and lacks support mail evidence.
Strong support mail evidence (8 emails) and sign_in hints have a proven positive track record (+2.9%).
Finish step has the highest drop-off (35.2%) and user confusion mail, though copy changes have shown mixed results.
Adoption changes generally succeed (+7.1%), targeting long step completion duration.
Addresses high wait duration (2336s mean), but home step changes have consistently underperformed.
